readings.title: The Selection of the Three Hundred
readings.subtitle: Gid'on's Army Reduced
readings.text: [Judges 7:1] Then Yerubbaʽal, that is Gidʽon, and all the people who were with him rose up early and encamped by the fountain of Ḥaroḏ. And the camp of Midian was on the north side of them, by the hill of Moreh in the valley. [2] And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> said to Gidʽon, <dq>“The people who are with you are too many for <dn>Me</dn> to give <dn>את</dn> Midian into their hands, lest Israel boast against <dn>Me</dn>, saying, ‘My own hand has saved me.’</dq> [3] <dq>“And now, proclaim in the hearing of the people, saying, ‘Whoever is afraid and trembling, let him turn back and leave Mount Gilʽaḏ.’ ”</dq> And twenty-two thousand of the people turned back, and ten thousand remained. [4] And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> said to Gidʽon, <dq>“The people are still too many. Bring <dn>את</dn> them down to the water, and let <dn>Me</dn> test them for you there. And it shall be, that of whom <dn>I</dn> say to you, ‘This one goes with you,’ let him go with you. And of whomever <dn>I</dn> say to you, ‘This one does not go with you,’ let him not go.”</dq> [5] So he brought <dn>את</dn> the people down to the water. And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> said to Gidʽon, <dq>“Everyone who laps from the water with his tongue, as a dog laps, separate <dn>את</dn> him from everyone who bows down on his knees to drink.”</dq> [6] And the number of those who lapped, putting their hand to their mouth, was three hundred men, but all the rest of the people bowed down on their knees to drink water. [7] And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> said to Gidʽon, <dq>“By the three hundred men who lapped <dn>I</dn> save you, and give <dn>את</dn> Midian into your hand. Let all the other people go, each to his place.”</dq> [8] So the people took <dn>את</dn> food and <dn>את</dn> their ram’s horns in their hands. And he sent away <dn>את</dn> all the rest of Israel, every man to his tent, and retained those three hundred men. Now the camp of Midian was below him in the valley. [9] And it came to be on that night that <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> said to him, <dq>“Arise, go down against the camp, for <dn>I</dn> have given it into your hand.</dq> [10] <dq>“But if you are afraid to go down, go down to the camp with Purah your servant,</dq> [11] <dq>“and you shall hear <dn>את</dn> what they say, and afterwards your hands shall be strengthened to go down against the camp.”</dq> So he went down with Purah his servant to the outpost of the armed men who were in the camp. [12] And Midian and Amalěq and all the people of the East were lying in the valley as numerous as locusts. And their camels were without number, as the sand by the seashore in multitude. [13] And Gidʽon came, and see, a man was relating a dream to his companion, and said, “See, I have dreamed a dream, and see, a cake of barley bread tumbled into the camp of Midian. And it came to a tent and struck it so that it fell and overturned, and the tent collapsed.” [14] And his companion answered and said, “This is nothing else but the sword of Gidʽon son of Joash, a man of Israel! <dn>Elohim</dn> has given <dn>את</dn> Midian and <dn>את</dn> all the camp into his hand.”

readings.title: The Sword of YeHoVaH and Gid'on
readings.subtitle: Defeat of the Midianites
readings.text: [15] And it came to be, when Gidʽon heard <dn>את</dn> the relating of the dream and <dn>את</dn> its interpretation, that he bowed himself in worship. And he returned to the camp of Israel, and said, “Arise, for <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> has given <dn>את</dn> the camp of Midian into your hand.” [16] And he divided <dn>את</dn> the three hundred men into three companies, and he put a ram’s horn into every man’s hand, with empty jars, and torches inside the jars. [17] And he said to them, “Look at me and do likewise. And see, when I come to the edge of the camp, do as I do. [18] “And I shall blow the ram’s horn, I and all who are with me, then you shall also blow the ram’s horns all around the camp, and say, ‘For <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> and for Gidʽon!’ ” [19] And Gidʽon and the hundred men who were with him came to the edge of the camp at the beginning of the middle watch, as they had but newly posted the watch. And they blew the ram’s horns and broke the jars that were in their hands. [20] And the three companies blew the ram’s horns and broke <dn>את</dn> the jars, and held the torches in their left hands and the ram’s horns in their right hands for blowing, and they cried, “The sword of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> and of Gidʽon!” [21] And each stood in his place all around the camp. And all the army ran and cried out and fled. [22] And the three hundred blew the ram’s horns, and <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> set <dn>את</dn> the sword of each one against his companion, even throughout all the army. And the army fled to Běyth Shittah, toward Tsererah, as far as the border of Aběl Meḥolah, by Tabbath. [23] And the men of Israel gathered together from Naphtali, and from Asher, and from all Menashsheh, and pursued Midian. [24] And Gidʽon sent messengers throughout all the mountains of Ephraim, saying, “Come down against Midian, and capture the watering places before them, as far as Běyth Barah and the Yarden.” So all the men of Ephraim gathered together and captured <dn>את</dn> the watering places, as far as Běyth Barah and the Yarden. [25] And they captured <dn>את</dn> two princes of the Midianites, <dn>את</dn> Orěḇ and <dn>את</dn> Ze’ěḇ. And they slew <dn>את</dn> Orěḇ at the rock of Orěḇ, and <dn>את</dn> Ze’ěḇ they slew at the winepress of Ze’ěḇ. And they pursued <dn>את</dn> Midian and brought the heads of Orěḇ and Ze’ěḇ to Gidʽon on the other side of the Yarden.

readings.title: Pursuing the Kings
readings.subtitle: Gid'on's Persistence
readings.text: [Judges 8:1] And the men of Ephraim said to him, “What is this deed you have done to us, not to call us when you went to fight against Midian?” And they contended with <dn>את</dn> him strongly. [2] And he said to them, “What have I done now in comparison with you? Is not the gleaning of grapes of Ephraim better than the vintage of Abiʽezer? [3] “<dn>Elohim</dn> has given <dn>את</dn> the princes of Midian, <dn>את</dn> Orěḇ and <dn>את</dn> Ze’ěḇ, into your hand, and what was I able to do in comparison with you?” Then their spirit toward him relaxed when he said that. [4] And Gidʽon came to the Yarden, he and the three hundred men who were with him, passing over, weary yet pursuing. [5] And he said to the men of Sukkoth, “Please give loaves of bread to the people who follow me, for they are weary, and I am pursuing Zeḇaḥ and Tsalmunna, sovereigns of Midian.” [6] And the leaders of Sukkoth said, “Are the hands of Zeḇaḥ and Tsalmunna now in your hand, that we should give bread to your army?” [7] And Gidʽon said, “For this, when <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> has given <dn>את</dn> Zeḇaḥ and <dn>את</dn> Tsalmunna into my hand, I shall thresh <dn>את</dn> your flesh with <dn>את</dn> the thorns of the wilderness and with <dn>את</dn> briers!” [8] And from there he went up to Penu’ěl and spoke to them in the same way. And the men of Penu’ěl answered him as the men of Sukkoth had answered. [9] And he also spoke to the men of Penu’ěl, saying, “When I come back in peace, I break down <dn>את</dn> this tower!” [10] Now Zeḇaḥ and Tsalmunna were at Qarqor, and their armies with them, about fifteen thousand, all who were left of all the army of the people of the East. For one hundred and twenty thousand men who drew the sword had fallen. [11] And Gidʽon went up by the way of those who dwell in tents on the east of Noḇah and Yogbehah, and smote <dn>את</dn> the army while the army thought it was safe. [12] And Zeḇaḥ and Tsalmunna fled, and he pursued them, and captured <dn>את</dn> the two sovereigns of Midian, <dn>את</dn> Zeḇaḥ and <dn>את</dn> Tsalmunna, and caused all the army to tremble. [13] And Gidʽon son of Joash returned from battle, from the ascent of Ḥeres. [14] And he caught a youth of the men of Sukkoth and asked him, and he wrote down for him <dn>את</dn> the leaders of Sukkoth and <dn>את</dn> the elders, seventy-seven men. [15] And he came to the men of Sukkoth and said, “See Zeḇaḥ and Tsalmunna, about whom you reproached <dn>את</dn> me, saying, ‘Are the hands of Zeḇaḥ and Tsalmunna now in your hand, that we should give bread to your weary men?’ ” [16] And he took <dn>את</dn> the elders of the city, and <dn>את</dn> thorns of the wilderness and <dn>את</dn> briers, and with them he taught <dn>את</dn> the men of Sukkoth. [17] And he broke down <dn>את</dn> the tower of Penu’ěl and slew <dn>את</dn> the men of the city. [18] And he said to Zeḇaḥ and Tsalmunna, “What kind of men were they whom you slew at Tabor?” And they answered, “As you are, so were they – everyone looked like the son of a sovereign.” [19] And he said, “They were my brothers, the sons of my mother. As <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> lives, if you had let them live, I would not kill you.” [20] And he said to Yether his first-born, “Rise, kill <dn>את</dn> them!” But the youth did not draw his sword, for he feared, because he was still a youth. [21] And Zeḇaḥ and Tsalmunna said, “Rise yourself, and fall upon us, for as a man is, so is his strength.” So Gidʽon rose and killed <dn>את</dn> Zeḇaḥ and <dn>את</dn> Tsalmunna, and took <dn>את</dn> the crescent ornaments that were on their camels’ necks.

readings.title: Gid'on's Snare
readings.subtitle: The Gold Ephod
readings.text: [22] And the men of Israel said to Gidʽon, “Rule over us, both you and your son, and your grandson also, for you have saved us from the hand of Midian.” [23] But Gidʽon said to them, “I do not rule over you, nor does my son rule over you. <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> rules over you.” [24] And Gidʽon said to them, “I have a request to make of you, that you give me, every man, the ear-rings of his booty.” For they had golden ear-rings, because they were Yishmaʽělites. [25] And they answered, “We shall certainly give!” And they spread out a garment, and each man threw into it the ear-rings of his booty. [26] And the weight of the gold ear-rings that he requested was one thousand seven hundred pieces of gold, besides the crescent ornaments, and the pendants, and the purple robes which were on the sovereigns of Midian, and besides the chains that were around their camels’ necks. [27] And Gidʽon made <dn>את</dn> it into an ephod and set it up in his city, in Ophrah. And all Israel went whoring after it there, and it became a snare to Gidʽon and to his house. [28] Thus Midian was humbled before the children of Israel, so that they lifted their heads no more. And the country rested forty years in the days of Gidʽon. [29] And Yerubbaʽal son of Joash went and dwelt in his own house. [30] And Gidʽon had seventy sons who came from his own body, for he had many wives. [31] And his concubine who was in Sheḵem, she also bore him a son, whose name he called <dn>את</dn> Abimelek. [32] And Gidʽon son of Joash died at a good old age, and was buried in the tomb of Joash his father, in Ophrah of the Abiʽezerites. [33] And it came to be, as soon as Gidʽon was dead, that the children of Israel again went whoring after the Baʽals, and made Baʽal-Berith their mighty one. [34] Thus the children of Israel did not remember <dn>את</dn> <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> their <dn>Elohim</dn>, who had delivered <dn>את</dn> them from the hands of all their enemies round about, [35] nor did they show kindness to the house of Yerubbaʽal, Gidʽon, according to all the good which he had done for Israel.

readings.title: Abimelek's Conspiracy
readings.subtitle: The Killing of the Seventy Sons
readings.text: [Judges 9:1] And Abimelek son of Yerubbaʽal went to Sheḵem, to his mother’s brothers, and spoke with <dn>את</dn> them and with <dn>את</dn> all the clan of the house of his mother’s father, saying, [2] “Please speak in the hearing of all the men of Sheḵem, ‘Which is better for you, that all seventy of the sons of Yerubbaʽal reign over you, or that one man reign over you?’ Remember that I am your own bone and flesh.” [3] And his mother’s brothers spoke all these words concerning him in the hearing of all the men of Sheḵem. And their heart was inclined to follow Abimelek, for they said, “He is our brother.” [4] And they gave him seventy pieces of silver from the house of Baʽal-Berith, with which Abimelek hired worthless and reckless men, and they followed him. [5] And he went to his father’s house at Ophrah and killed <dn>את</dn> his brothers, <dn>את</dn> the seventy sons of Yerubbaʽal, on one stone. But Jotham the youngest son of Yerubbaʽal was left, because he hid himself. [6] And all the men of Sheḵem gathered together, and all of Běyth Millo, and they went and made <dn>את</dn> Abimelek sovereign beside the terebinth tree of the monument that was in Sheḵem.

readings.title: Jotham's Parable
readings.subtitle: The Trees Anoint a King
readings.text: [7] And they told Jotham, so he went and stood on top of Mount Gerizim, and lifted his voice and cried out. And he said to them, “Listen to me, you men of Sheḵem, and let <dn>Elohim</dn> listen to you! [8] “The trees once went forth to anoint a sovereign over them. And they said to the olive tree, ‘Reign over us!’ [9] “But the olive tree said to them, ‘Should I cease <dn>את</dn> my fatness, with which by me they esteem <dn>Elohim</dn> and men, and go to wave over trees?’ [10] “Then the trees said to the fig tree, ‘You come, reign over us!’ [11] “But the fig tree said to them, ‘Should I cease <dn>את</dn> my sweetness and <dn>את</dn> my good fruit, and go to wave over trees?’ [12] “Then the trees said to the vine, ‘You come, reign over us!’ [13] “But the vine said to them, ‘Should I cease <dn>את</dn> my new wine, which cheers <dn>Elohim</dn> and men, and go to wave over trees?’ [14] “Then all the trees said to the bramble, ‘You come, reign over us!’ [15] “And the bramble said to the trees, ‘If in truth you anoint <dn>את</dn> me as sovereign over you, come, take refuge in my shade. But if not, let fire come out of the bramble and devour <dn>את</dn> the cedars of Lebanon!’ [16] “And now, if you have acted in truth and integrity in making <dn>את</dn> Abimelek sovereign, and if you have dealt well with Yerubbaʽal and his house, and have done to him as his hands deserved – [17] for my father fought for you, and risked <dn>את</dn> his life, and delivered <dn>את</dn> you out of the hand of Midian, [18] but you have risen up against my father’s house this day, and killed <dn>את</dn> his seventy sons on one stone, and made <dn>את</dn> Abimelek, the son of his female servant, sovereign over the men of Sheḵem, because he is your brother – [19] if then you have acted in truth and integrity with Yerubbaʽal and with his house this day, rejoice in Abimelek, and let him also rejoice in you. [20] “But if not, let fire come out from Abimelek and devour <dn>את</dn> the men of Sheḵem and Běyth Millo, and let fire come out from the men of Sheḵem and from Běyth Millo and devour <dn>את</dn> Abimelek!” [21] And Jotham ran away and fled, and went to Be’ěr and dwelt there, for fear of Abimelek his brother.
